newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK Mortgage Corp seen launching late 1997 - HKMA.
newsitem.headline: HK Mortgage Corp seen launching late 1997 - HKMA.

text.p: Hong Kong's Mortgage Corporation should be operational by late this year, a Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) spokesman said on Thursday.
"We are on schedule," a spokesman said, adding that the HKMA expected to finalise staff recruitment and offices for the Mortgage Corp by the end of August.

The HKMA, Hong Kong's de facto central bank, will run the Mortgage Corp, which is aimed at helping ease the mismatch of funding between long-term lending and short-term borrowing and improve financing flows for home ownership.
Some banks have recently securitised mortgages to free up their balance sheets, rather than wait for the Mortgage Corp, which was originally expected to be in operation by mid-1997.
The Hong Kong arm of Sanwa International Finance completed a US$144 million residential mortgage-backed securities issue last week, part of its Hong Kong residential mortgage portfolio.
Sanwa's deal was the first cross-border AAA/Aaa rated mortgage-backed securities issue collateralised by residential mortgages originated in Hong Kong, Sanwa said.
Dah Sing Financial Holdings Ltd is also holding a roadshow on Thursday on a planned mortgage-backed securitisation.
